saints.name: St. Anthony of Egypt
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: The father of Christian monasticism, who gave away all he had and went out to seek God in the desert…
biography: Born about 251 at Coma in Lower Egypt of well-to-do Christian parents, Anthony was left at twenty with his sister and an estate. Hearing in church, 'Go, sell what you have and give to the poor', he gave away his lands, placed his sister among virgins, and put himself under an aged hermit.

After years among the tombs, wrestling with demons, he shut himself about 285 in an old fort at Pispir for twenty years; emerging about 305, he guided the disciples gathered round it, and from that colony grew the monasticism of the desert. His last decades he passed on the Inner Mountain by the Red Sea, where his monastery stands.

Twice he broke his solitude: about 311 to strengthen the Christians imprisoned at Alexandria, and in 338 to preach beside Athanasius against the Arians. The Life by Athanasius carried his fame everywhere and helped convert Augustine. He died on 17 January 356, aged one hundred and five.

Father of monks, he is their patron; of domestic animals he is patron because the Hospitallers of Saint Anthony, who nursed the sickness called Saint Anthony's fire, kept pigs that roamed the streets, whence the pig at his side in art.
saints.knownFor: Being the father of Christian monasticism.
